component.name: OdyTTY
component.summary: GPU-rendered terminal emulator with an Odyssey visual identity

description.p: OdyTTY is a from-scratch Rust terminal emulator for Linux. It owns the terminal byte path from PTY allocation through escape parsing, terminal state, render geometry, and GPU presentation.
The project explores a distinctive Odyssey visual identity while keeping terminal correctness, readable text, predictable input, local privacy, and performance as hard requirements.

screenshot.caption: OdyTTY running a shell with the Odyssey visual identity

description.p: Cursor, selection, and multi-pane hardening release, and the first with Windows install channels (Scoop and winget). Fixes resize cursor drift on pulled scrollback, minimize/restore black-screen and 1x1 reflow, prompt-aware select+Delete surviving a side-by-side split, clickable paths for filenames containing spaces, multi-pane wheel scrolling the pane under the cursor and hover resolving to the correct pane, drag-selection after a split, and a divider-drag pseudoconsole resize flood. Adds PowerShell shell integration (OSC 133 marks) and OSC 7 working-directory reporting on Windows. Interactive Windows behaviour is validated on-device; Linux, macOS, and Windows are all blocking CI legs.

First experimental Windows build: OdyTTY compiles and runs on Windows through a ConPTY pseudoconsole backend, shipping as an unsigned portable x86_64 zip alongside the existing source, AppImage, and AUR artifacts. Local tabs, splits, rendering, themes, effects, inline graphics, and persistent configuration under %APPDATA% work; detachable/resumable session hosting stays Unix-only for this release.
Fixes settings-description drift so each setting's help text matches its actual behaviour, and restores the GUI "reset to default background" action.
Ships a bundled default background and OdysseyOS identity defaults, so a fresh install opens with the intended Odyssey visual identity out of the box.

Adds an in-app About section to the settings overlay: a read-only view (the last row of the settings list) showing version, build provenance (git commit, build date, target, Rust version), and live GPU/renderer diagnostics (adapter, backend, driver), plus clickable project links and a one-click "Copy diagnostics" for bug reports. The diagnostics block deliberately omits filesystem paths so it can be shared without leaking a username.

Adds two opt-in ergonomic features and keyboard parity for prompt editing: a smart Ctrl+C mode (copy-or-interrupt) that copies a local selection when one exists and otherwise sends the interrupt, clickable bare URLs (Ctrl+click to open printed http/https links, on by default), and Delete/Backspace removing a selected editable prompt input via the same shell-integration-gated path as the right-click Delete. Ships a best-effort x86_64 AppImage and an AUR package alongside the source release.

One-fix patch release: the native window now announces its application id (io.unfinished_works.odytty) on Linux, so Wayland compositors and X11 bars resolve the OdyTTY taskbar/dock icon instead of a generic placeholder. The desktop file gains a matching StartupWMClass so spawned windows group under their launcher entry.

Visual-polish release: Nerd Font / symbol icon glyphs are now scaled aspect-preserving and centered in their cell so icon columns (e.g. a fastfetch panel) render even and uncropped, while body text stays byte-identical. OdyTTY also self-identifies to terminal-aware tooling by exporting TERM_PROGRAM=odytty and TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION.

Bug-fix and UX release validated hands-on on both Linux and macOS: click-to-open now works on a real desktop (Ctrl+click on Linux, Cmd+click on macOS), closing the v0.4.0 cross-platform regressions, and extends the interactive-paths workflow layer.

Brings multi-tab and split-pane multiplexing (each pane keeps its own scrollback, selection, viewport, and search), detached resumable sessions with reattach driven by a local-only, per-user Unix socket, and an in-window Manage Sessions overlay (default Ctrl+Shift+A) for attach, rename, kill, and Detach and switch. Adds an SSH connection manager, a Ctrl+Shift+P command palette, and a scrubbable session-replay overlay. Introduces interactive paths (default off): with the gate enabled, OdyTTY detects filesystem paths in its output and Ctrl+click opens them — files via xdg-open, path:line:col via an editor matrix, directories via the file manager — plus Open, Open With…, Copy Path, Copy File, and Reveal in File Manager context items. Resolved image paths open in an in-app lightbox viewer (Esc or click-outside to dismiss). The in-panel keybinding editor now covers every bindable action.

Makes four overlays discoverable by giving each a default Ctrl+Shift chord and a menu entry: Ctrl+Shift+P opens the command palette, Ctrl+Shift+S the connection manager, Ctrl+Shift+R the session-replay overlay, and Ctrl+Shift+B the theme builder. All four use Ctrl+Shift+<letter> chords that a TUI cannot receive, so no PTY input path is perturbed, and every chord remains rebindable. Prompt navigation stays on the Ctrl+Shift+Up / Ctrl+Shift+Down arrow chords.

Lands native splits and panes on a per-tab binary layout tree (single-pane tabs stay byte-identical), reachable via tmux-style prefix bindings and direct Ctrl+Shift+E / Ctrl+Shift+O chords with drag-resizable dividers and directional focus moves. Adds resumable, persistent sessions: a detached session-host process owns the PTYs and terminal models so a window can close and reattach with full scrollback over a per-user, local-only Unix socket, with CLI verbs odytty new, list, and attach. Also introduces an SSH connection manager and a command palette.

Fixes insert/replace mode (IRM, ANSI mode 4): printing in insert mode now shifts existing cells to the right instead of overwriting them, so editors that rely on incremental line redraw — notably Apple's pico/nano on macOS — no longer corrupt the current line. Also bounds scrollback memory by default (a runaway program can no longer grow history until the system runs out of memory) and makes the test suite deterministic. No change to terminal behavior beyond the IRM fix.

Adds a mouse-cursor shape (an I-beam over the text grid, a hand over hyperlinks, an arrow over chrome), fixes a stuck-underline bug from a misparsed private-mode escape sequence, and improves macOS symbol-glyph and color coverage. OdyTTY now ships as source only on both Linux and macOS: the prebuilt macOS disk image is retired in favor of a build-from-source flow, and both platforms are exercised in continuous integration.

Fixes scrollback not filling when a program leaves a full-screen scroll region set (so the mouse wheel and Shift+PageUp could not scroll back), adds alternate scroll mode so the wheel scrolls full-screen TUIs like pagers, discovers Apple Color Emoji on macOS, persists first-run onboarding dismissal, and builds from source on older stable Rust toolchains.
Adds an experimental universal macOS build and a tag-triggered release pipeline that publishes the Linux source archive and the macOS disk image together. No functional change for Linux.
Adds bell handling (visual flash or window urgency, configurable) and IME composition input so CJK input methods and compose-key accents work.
Makes the bundled Nerd Font glyph pack render across both v2 and v3 codepoint eras via an ordered symbol fallback chain, and groups the font picker into bundled and system fonts.
Adds geometric Unicode Braille pattern rendering so btop and other Braille-graph terminal output does not fall back to missing-glyph boxes.
Fixes uneven background-image opacity in the padding and non-grid edge regions when translucent cell backgrounds are enabled.
Adds `odytty -e command args...`, `--working-directory`, and `--title` launch support for terminal-exec integrations and command launchers.
Fixes a native-session shutdown crash that could panic after the final shell exited while the event loop was still processing teardown.
Refreshes the public README install guide so the release archive matches the documented user-local install flow.
Initial Linux pre-release target with source packaging, desktop launcher metadata, and hicolor icon assets.
